uncited: The CUDA Rasterization Backward Kernel computes the gradients of the rasterization loss with respect to the input vertex positions and other geometric parameters, enabling end-to-end differentiable voxelization.
It serves as the reverse-mode counterpart to the forward rasterization kernel, propagating gradients from the volume space back to the mesh or point cloud representation.

Unlike the forward pass which accumulates color/opacity into a volume, this kernel distributes gradients from the volume buffer to the vertex attributes, supporting optimization of 3D structures from 2D projections or volume targets.

The kernel implements the chain rule to compute $\frac{\partial L}{\partial \text{vertices}}$ and $\frac{\partial L}{\partial \text{other params}}$ given the upstream gradient $\frac{\partial L}{\partial \text{volume}}$.
- `grad_volume`: Tensor of shape $(W, H, D)$ or flattened equivalent, containing $\frac{\partial L}{\partial \text{volume}_{w,h,d}}$.
**Gradient Computation (Render):** The backward render kernel is called to compute gradients with respect to the mean position, conic matrix, and opacity.
**Covariance Selection:** The pointer to the 3D covariance matrix is selected.
Typical values depend on the scene resolution (e.g., 256x256x256).
The Voxelizer Backward Pass is the high-level function that orchestrates the backward computation for the entire voxelization pipeline.
It reconstructs state objects from buffers, handles default radii, and calls the specific backward render and preprocess kernels.
It is chosen when optimizing geometric parameters (vertices, scales, rotations) from volume-based losses.
- **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of volume voxels and primitives, $O(W \cdot H \cdot D + N \cdot M)$, where $N$ is the number of vertices and $M$ is the number of faces.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(W \cdot H \cdot D)$ for the volume buffer and gradients, plus $O(N + M)$ for vertex and face data.
- **Performance:** Performance is highly dependent on the volume resolution and the efficiency of the spatial hashing/binning structures.
Precision issues may require higher precision types.
The CUDA Rasterization Backward Kernel is part of the differentiable voxelization pipeline used in 3D reconstruction and optimization tasks.
It was developed as part of the `voxel2mesh` and `r2_gaussian` projects, which aim to optimize 3D meshes and Gaussian splats from 2D projections or volume data.
